changes_made.explanation: Normalized model names to standard forms, consolidated duplicate dataset entries, and added explicit model specifications. Maintained 'Other (10 total languages)' category since specific languages beyond the main 5 are not explicitly named in the paper text.
Consolidated duplicate metrics (MRR, precision) and normalized all metric names to standard capitalized forms. Simplified variants to base forms (e.g., ROUGE-1/2/3 become just ROUGE).
Removed placeholder 'None' values since no LLM-as-judge evaluation was conducted. The paper does not use LLMs for evaluation purposes.

guideline: Human annotators were asked to select the set with more responses that they prefer to send as a reply

changes_made.explanation: The extracted metadata was accurate. Human evaluation was conducted using preference judgments between generation and retrieval model outputs on English data only.

overall_notes: The paper presents a comprehensive study comparing generation vs. retrieval models for multilingual reply suggestion. The extraction quality was generally good with minor normalization needed. Key findings: (1) Generation models perform better on English but struggle with cross-lingual transfer, (2) Retrieval models generalize better across languages, (3) Different cross-lingual strategies work best for each model type. The paper uses both automatic metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, etc.) and human preference evaluations.
